title: Add multi-window burn-rate alerting recording rules + alert queries (tiered SLOs)
author: Sergio Costa
description:
This PR introduces the first cut of multi-window, multi-burn-rate alerting for tiered SLOs (Hosted vs Dedicated) using Prometheus recording rules + Alertmanager alerts. The goal is to standardize burn-rate paging across endpoint classes (chat/completions, embeddings, streaming) and regions without blowing up cardinality. This is the alerting layer for the tiered SLO + error budget program; budget computation/enforcement gates are tracked separately.

What’s included: (1) Recording rules to compute request success rate and burn rate from gateway/routing SLIs with consistent label sets (tier, region, route_class, protocol). (2) Alert queries implementing multi-window burn-rate alerts (fast + slow) per tier/endpoint/region with initial thresholds aligned to a 30d budget window. (3) Alert annotations with runbook + dashboard links and incident-bot-friendly fields. (4) Guardrails to avoid per-model/per-customer label expansion (we intentionally do NOT include model_id or customer_id in the core paging alerts).

Key design points: (a) Alerts page on burn rate (error budget consumption) rather than raw error rate to normalize across SLO targets. (b) Multi-window alerts reduce flapping and catch both sharp regressions and slow leaks. (c) Tier-aware labeling is required at ingest (see tier-tagging PR); this PR assumes the tier label is present on the underlying SLI metrics.

Initial thresholds (subject to tuning during rollout): For 30d SLO windows, we page when burn_rate_1h > 14.4 AND burn_rate_5m > 14.4 (fast burn), or burn_rate_6h > 6 AND burn_rate_30m > 6 (slow burn). These are standard Google SRE-style burn alerts and correspond to spending a material fraction of the monthly budget quickly. We emit warning (Slack only) at half thresholds to support the warn-only enforcement phase.

Runbooks / dashboards: Runbook: confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/error-budget-breach-mitigation-runbook. Dashboard: grafana/d/tiered-slo/tiered-slo-burn-rate (linked in annotations). Incident process: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/error-budget-breach-incident-process.

Notes / follow-ups: (1) Streaming disconnect SLI semantics are still being finalized; current alerting uses the existing stream_error_total / stream_sessions_total series with client-abort exclusions applied upstream. (2) Dedicated account-level alerts are out of scope here; this PR only covers tier/region/route_class aggregates. (3) Once enforcement gates move beyond warn-only, we’ll revisit severities + paging routes per tier.

Test plan: Validated rule evaluation in promtool; verified generated series names/labels in staging; manually triggered an error-rate spike in staging gateway to confirm fast-burn paging + annotation links; validated Alertmanager routing to eng-sre-oncall for Dedicated and eng-platform-oncall for Hosted (as configured in alertmanager routes).

Risk: Moderate. Recording rules are additive but can increase TSDB load if label sets drift; we included explicit labeldrop/labelkeep in rule templates and limited dimensions to tier/region/route_class/protocol only.
commits: observability: add base SLI aggregation recording rules for tier/region/route_class
alerts: add burn-rate recording rules (5m/30m/1h/6h) for availability + streaming reliability
alerts: add multi-window burn-rate alerts with severities + routing labels
dashboards: add deploy/incident annotations hook fields used by burn alerts
docs: link runbook + dashboard in alert annotations; add notes on exclusions
implementation_notes: Burn rate definition: burn_rate = (1 - success_rate) / (1 - slo_target). For streaming: burn_rate = stream_failure_rate / allowed_failure_rate (target varies by tier).
We use recording rules to normalize names: redwood:sli_success_rate:<window> and redwood:slo_burn_rate:<window> with a stable label set.
alert_examples: Warning (slack): same queries with thresholds /2 and severity=warning
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we confirm the label set won’t accidentally include model_id after the routing layer adds tags? I want this to be safe-by-default.

Sergio Costa: Yep—recording rules explicitly use by(tier, region, route_class, protocol). Even if upstream adds model_id/customer_id, it won’t be preserved in the aggregate series. I also added a template helper to labeldrop everything except the allowlist for the final series name.
Thomas Baird: These recording rules will create a lot of series if route_class is too granular. What values do we expect here? Please document the allowlist.

Sergio Costa: Good call. Updated docs to define route_class as one of {chat, completions, embeddings, rerank, streaming} and added a prom rule test that fails if new classes appear without updating the allowlist.

Aisha Bello: Thresholds look reasonable, but for Hosted we may need to start with warning-only paging during rollout. Can we set severity=page only for Dedicated and warning for Hosted for the first week?

Sergio Costa: I wired severity mapping by tier behind a single variable in the alert config. Default is page for both, but I added a staged override file (disabled by default) we can enable in prod during rollout.
Connor O'Brien: Please add runbook link + dashboard link in annotations; incident-bot depends on consistent annotation keys.
Sergio Costa: Added annotations: runbook_url, dashboard_url, slo_tier, route_class, region, and a short 'impact' string. Also aligned summary formatting with incident-bot expectations.
Logan Wright: Any concerns about scraping/evaluation load? Also, do we have promtool coverage for these rules?
Sergio Costa: Added promtool rule tests for recording + alert rules (synthetic fixtures) and confirmed CPU impact is within limits in staging (<3% evaluator CPU increase).
release_notes: Internal: Added tier-aware multi-window burn-rate alerting rules/alerts for Hosted and Dedicated SLOs with runbook + dashboard links. No customer-facing changes.
